articles.title: Your AI Feature’s Bill Has More Lines Than the Model Invoice
articles.excerpt: You Budget for a Request, but You Pay for a System Ask a team what their AI feature will cost, and you’ll usually get a calculation: requests per day, multiplied by tokens per request, multiplied by t…
articles.body: You Budget for a Request, but You Pay for a System Ask a team what their AI feature will cost, and you’ll usually get a calculation: requests per day, multiplied by tokens per request, multiplied by the provider’s rate. It’s a reasonable starting point and almost always an underestimate. The model invoice covers one component. The feature itself is a system: data pipelines feeding it context, people checking its output, controls keeping it secure, accounts and keys that need managing, and an owner who keeps it working as models and data change. Each of those has a cost, and most don’t appear on any provider’s pricing page. If you’re approving budget for an AI feature, or reviewing a vendor’s estimate, here’s where the rest of the bill comes from.
articles.author: RWaltz Software

articles.title: ARIA defines exactly one live region role that stays silent by default, and it is the one we set aria-live on
articles.excerpt: Our quiz app shows the same countdown twice: once on the host's screen behind the bar, and once on every player's phone. Same clock, same seconds, two separate components written months apart. One of…
articles.body: Our quiz app shows the same countdown twice: once on the host's screen behind the bar, and once on every player's phone. Same clock, same seconds, two separate components written months apart. One of them talks to a screen reader every single second. The other says nothing at all. Neither is right, and the pair of them is a decent illustration of what live regions are for. The host's countdown < span className = "tabular-nums text-4xl font-bold transition-colors duration-300 ..." role = "timer" aria-live = "polite" aria-label = { ` ${ remaining } seconds remaining` } > { remaining } </ span > remaining is recomputed from the server clock on a one second interval, so both the text node and the aria-label are replaced on every tick, for the whole answer window.

articles.title: Add an AI agent that remembers your users, with one REST call
articles.excerpt: Most "add AI to your support" tutorials stop at a chat completion. The model answers, and then you discover the real work: remembering who the user is between messages, answering from your documents i…
articles.body: Most "add AI to your support" tutorials stop at a chat completion. The model answers, and then you discover the real work: remembering who the user is between messages, answering from your documents instead of the internet, knowing when a message is a hot lead, booking a slot without double-booking, and not charging twice when your client retries a request. We built all of that for our own product, an AI agent that answers customers on WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger, Telegram, email and website chat. The same engine is available as a REST API, so you can run it inside your own app without any of those channels. This post shows what one call looks like and what comes back.

articles.title: Where to Put the Human Check When You Combine Jira Automation and AI
articles.excerpt: Automation rules do exactly what you tell them. AI-generated text and queries can be close but not quite right. Put them together and a small error can repeat across hundreds of issues. Short answer:…
articles.body: Automation rules do exactly what you tell them. AI-generated text and queries can be close but not quite right. Put them together and a small error can repeat across hundreds of issues. Short answer: let AI draft, let a person approve, and only then let automation act. Pattern 1: Draft, then review If a rule posts an AI-written summary to a ticket, have it post as an internal comment first. A person reads it and decides whether to share it with the customer. Pattern 2: Test on a narrow scope When a rule uses a generated query, run it on one project, or add a label condition, before widening it. Check the audit log after the first few runs. Pattern 3: Don't automate irreversible actions Bulk transitions, deletions and customer-facing emails should wait for a person's sign-off.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.excerpt: Before it leaves HBO, revisit one of Tom Cruise’s richest and most emotionally resonant character studies.
articles.body: Tom Cruise has built a career out of playing larger-than-life characters, but some of his best performances are when he delves into the more vulnerable people beneath the movie-star bravado. Days of Thunder filters the story of a hotshot NASCAR driver through the humbling process of learning to trust someone, while Jerry Maguire finds a sports agent in the throes of learning that success means little without genuine human connection. Even Tropic Thunder , for all its outrageous comedy, gives Cruise room to disappear into a grotesque Hollywood executive whose insecurities are as ridiculous as his explosive temper. And Alejandro González Iñárritu’s Digger gives Cruise one of his most fascinating character studies yet as an oil tycoon with a brazen plan to save the world.

articles.body: Japan's mission to Mars is one of the most ambitious in spaceflight history. It aims to become the first spacecraft to return to Earth from Mars orbit, carrying with it the first-ever samples from the Red Planet system. articles.title: Computer scientist Margaret Hamilton was a problem-solver for the ages (op-ed)
articles.excerpt: The world will miss Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering programmer who helped NASA land Apollo astronauts on the moon. But we will always have her example to inspire us.
articles.body: Dean Robbins is a journalist and children's author. He contributed this article to Space.com's Expert Voices: Op-Ed & Insights . The pioneering computer scientist Margaret Hamilton , who died on Sept. 30 at age 90, played a key role in putting astronauts on the moon. She was a problem-solver extraordinaire, and it all started in early childhood. Considering the name "daddy longlegs" unfair to female arachnids, young Margaret decided to call half of them "mommy longlegs." Wondering why the neighborhood baseball players were all boys, she determined to join the team herself. As she grew up in the 1940s and '50s, Margaret noticed a similar problem with various professions. Why were doctors, judges and scientists almost always men?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 18, 1963: France's Félicette Becomes the 1st Cat in Space! >^..^<
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 18, 1963, a cat went to space! Félicette was a French "catstronaut" who became the first and only feline to fly to space. While the U.S. and Soviet Union were busy launching primates, dogs and humans, the French decided to join the space race by launching a cat. Félicette, a stray tuxedo cat from the streets of Paris, was a substitute for another cat named Felix, who somehow escaped on launch day. So Félicette went where no cat had ever gone before. She boarded a French Véronique AG1 rocket and soared 130 miles above the Earth before safely parachuting back down. Luckily Félicette made it home alive and well, unlike many of the other animal astronauts that flew during the space race. Félicette, the first cat to fly into space in October 1963, is seen her carrier pre-flight.

articles.title: Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way
articles.excerpt: A citizen science project is seeking volunteers to comb through NASA telescope data for telltale signs of the galaxy's hidden black holes.
articles.body: Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70. Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters , is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole , volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
